Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward with the POC. Legal and InfoSec asked me to gather some concrete commitments and evidence before we onboard any production-like traffic. At a high level they want:

- A firm commitment that ZephyrHealth data will not be used to improve or fine-tune any Redwood models for the duration of this POC (and clear language on what happens afterwards).
- Clarification on prompt/response entitlements — specifically whether outputs generated by the model are considered customer-owned and whether we can export transcripts and embeddings.
- A list of subprocessors and the ability to confirm the POC will run in a dedicated environment (or an equivalent isolation guarantee).
- Operational evidence: SOC2 report location, sample audit log export (tokenized), and a technical note on how KV/prefix caching is handled and whether prompts are retained in persistent storage.

I've attached the security questionnaire our team filled (security_questionnaire.pdf) with some targeted asks. Can you confirm what Redwood can provide and an ETA for evidence artifacts?

We'd prefer the initial commitments in writing (email or a short addendum). If there's a template clause Redwood can accept, that would speed things up.

Best,
Marta Reyes
Senior Procurement Manager
ZephyrHealth

--

Hi Marta — great to hear the team is ready. Appreciate the detailed questionnaire.

Short answers up front:
- Commitment: For the POC we can commit in writing that ZephyrHealth data will not be used to improve or train any Redwood models (no-model-improvement) while the POC is live. We can provide a one-paragraph addendum that you can attach to the DPA.
- Prompt/response entitlements: Outputs (responses & generated embeddings) will be exportable to ZephyrHealth as part of the POC. We assert no claim over customer outputs for the duration of the agreement.
- Isolation & subprocessors: We can run the POC on a Dedicated project (reserved capacity) or in a logically isolated private deployment depending on your preference; both options support data residence controls and KMS integration. We'll supply a current subprocessor list and SOC2 reference.
- Operational evidence: We will produce a short evidence pack (SOC2 reference, subprocessor attestation, sample audit-log export, and an ops note on KV/prefix caching behavior).

Next steps I'd propose:
1) I can send a proposed DPA addendum this afternoon with the training-exclusion paragraph and the prompt/output ownership language.
2) My ops partner will prepare the evidence pack (ETA: 3 business days) and an ops whitepaper that documents ephemeral KV behavior and retention settings.
3) If you'd like us to host the POC on Dedicated capacity that will be provisioned once commercial terms are finalized — let me know which you prefer.

Looping in our Legal & Ops folks to coordinate the artifacts — david_kim@redwood.com (legal), kimberly_park@redwood.com (security), priyom_das@redwood.com (ops).

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

--
